body: Since the value of `configuration` can change I don't think we can actually call this `[SameObject]` but the getter steps for the attribute are good enough to specify the behavior we want.

body:
Now that we have `[[configurationValue]]` and `[[selectedAlternateSetting]]` we don't need to have this definition for an "active configuration". We can define explicit algorithms for finding interfaces and endpoints in the active configuration like this step from `transferIn()`:

> Let endpoint be the IN endpoint in the [active configuration](https://pr-preview.s3.amazonaws.com/chengweih001/webusb/pull/212.html#active-configuration) with bEndpointAddress corresponding to endpointNumber. If there is no such endpoint [reject](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#reject) promise with a [NotFoundError](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notfounderror) and abort these steps.

Remove "to" from the name of the algorithm so that the language is less awkward when invoking it.

```suggestion
<div algorithm="find the device descriptor for the connected usb device">
    To <dfn>find the device descriptor for the connected usb device</dfn>,
```

USB is always capitalized.

```suggestion
<div algorithm="find a list of configuration descriptors for the connected USB device">
    To <dfn>find a list of configuration descriptors for the connected USB device</dfn>,
```

I think these algorithms should state the assumption that these descriptors have already been read from the device as part of originally enumerating the device. This is how Chromium implements it and there's no need to imply that the data would be re-requested for any of these steps.
There is no target `USBDevice` object for this algorithm. Add *device* as a second parameter to these steps.

Actually, it kind of links to the issue of https://github.com/tabatkins/bikeshed/issues/2225. In order to get around the errors, I moved around as in https://github.com/chengweih001/webusb_sameobject_patch/commit/6b111b1b5a5f1955752f4084d552b023002f1d78.

And this move around ended up not wrapping the |configuration| parameter in dfn tag within algorithm tag, then bikeshed complains no reference for the variable as it ends up only be referenced once.

I will add ignore to those variable and remove those non-necessary parameter assignment lines, let me know if you think with this reason it is fine to keep those.

body:
Yeah, as they said, there's a Bikeshed bug currently where wrapping markdown dt/dds in a div (that is a child of a dl) doesn't get detected and corrected properly, so it retains the generated dl wrapper and emits bad HTML. I'll be fixing it shortly; then the algorithm wrapper can be put back around the dt/dd pair.

Or you can structure the html to not use a dt/dd pairs for the operations, and instead just make them flat `<div algorithm>`s that name the operation being defined in an intro paragraph, like in <https://drafts.css-houdini.org/css-typed-om/#dom-cssnumericvalue-add>

Let me know how I think by specifying it in this way.

If we were putting the name of the algorithm in quotes then I agree "aborting" is more grammatically correct but in this case we can remove the word "perform" entirely and say,
